title: Yam Porridge with Smoked Fish
author: Fafa Gilbert
desc: Four hundred grams of yam to seven hundred millilitres of water with two smoked fish and five green chillies — spare, and its method is video-only.
longDesc: The plainest documented mpotompoto: four hundred grams of cubed yam, seven hundred millilitres of water, two large smoked fish, one onion, five green chillies and salt. That is the whole list. Garnished with six whole green chillies and a sliced onion. It makes a useful counterpoint to the elaborate versions — no bell pepper, no tomato, no crayfish, no bouillon — just yam, water, smoked fish and heat. The author's one printed tip is about the oil: ensure your palm oil is sustainably produced, and it is best to use zomi for this recipe.
ingredients: // Noted in the author's tip but not in the ingredient list
steps: // The published method for this recipe is video-only. No written steps exist in the source.
Bring the water to the boil with the onion and chillies.
Add the yam and simmer until tender.
Mash part of the yam to thicken the porridge, leaving some cubes whole.
Season with salt and finish with zomi.
Garnish with the whole green chillies and sliced onion.
// The order and timings above are inferred from the other documented mpotompoto, not from this source.
chefTips: Be aware the method here is reconstructed. The source publishes a full ingredient list but its instructions are in a video, so the step order follows the other documented mpotompoto rather than this cook's own sequence.
Seven hundred millilitres of water to four hundred grams of yam is the only documented liquid ratio for this dish, and it is the reason this sparse entry is worth having.
Her tip as printed: ensure your palm oil is sustainably produced, and it is best to use zomi for this recipe. Note the oil is not in her ingredient list at all.
Eleven green chillies in total — five in the pot, six as garnish. That is a lot, and they are mild green chillies rather than scotch bonnet.
Whole chillies as a garnish is an Ewe habit and they are eaten alongside rather than stirred in.
No tomato, no bell pepper, no crayfish, no bouillon. This is yam, water, fish and heat, and it is a genuinely different dish from the elaborate version at GHA034.
Two large smoked fish for four servings makes this very fish-forward. The smoke is the seasoning.
commonMistakes: Treating the reconstructed step order as the author's own.
Leaving out the zomi because it is not in the ingredient list.
Using scotch bonnet in place of mild green chillies.
Adding tomato, which belongs to the other version.
sources: Quantities from 'The Ghanaian Yam Porridge (Mpotompoto)', byline as printed 'Fafa Gilbert', 1 October 2018. Fafa Gilbert is Ewe, from the Volta Region, per her own site — the basis for the community attribution.
Ingredients exactly as printed: 2 large smoked fish; 1 large onion; 5 green chillies; 400g peeled and cubed yam pieces; 700ml water; salt. Garnish: 6 whole green chillies, 1 sliced onion.

METHOD GAP, stated plainly: NO WRITTEN METHOD AND NO DONENESS CUE exist in the source. The instructions are published as a YouTube video. The steps in this entry are explicitly marked as reconstructed from the other documented mpotompoto (GHA034), and the step list carries a header saying so. Nothing in the step order is attributed to this author.

THE AUTHOR'S TIP, verbatim: 'Please ensure your Palm oil is sustainably produced and it is best to use Zomi for this recipe.' NOTE THE DISCREPANCY: palm oil appears in her tip but NOT in her ingredient list, so its quantity is genuinely missing. It is carried in the ingredient list above under a header noting this, with no amount asserted.

WHY IT IS PUBLISHED DESPITE THE METHOD GAP: the 400 g yam to 700 ml water ratio is the only documented liquid-to-yam figure for mpotompoto anywhere in the material consulted, and the ingredient list is so much sparer than the other version that it documents a genuinely different approach to the dish rather than a variation on one.

CONTRAST WITH THE OTHER DOCUMENTED VERSION, recorded rather than reconciled: GHA034 uses red bell peppers, plum tomatoes, garlic, habanero, dried herring, ground crayfish, bouillon powder, chicken broth and sweet potato alongside the yam. This version uses none of those. Both are published as mpotompoto because both sources call them that.

ON ZOMI: palm oil processed further than ordinary red palm oil, darker and more strongly flavoured. Both documented mpotompoto sources specify zomi rather than generic palm oil, which is a point of agreement worth noting given how little else they share.
reheating: Low heat with water to loosen.
healthBenefits: Yam supplies potassium, vitamin C and a lower glycaemic load than potato.
Smoked fish provides protein, omega-3 fats and iodine.
Very little added fat as written.
Green chillies are high in vitamin C.
culturalNote: A list this short tells you the dish is everyday food rather than company food — yam, water, whatever fish is hanging in the kitchen, and chillies on the side for whoever wants them. The whole green chillies set beside the bowl rather than cooked in is a habit you see across the Volta Region.
